headline: Sector Strike: Speak Coordinates and Claim the Grid
problemStatement: Team quiz games can make recall lively, but students also need visible reasons to coordinate and explain their choices. Sector Strike combines questions with territory: two teams answer, choose a location on an 8-by-8 board, and try to connect four claimed sectors in a row.
outcomes: Review speaking and recall while competing toward a shared team goal.
Practice calling grid coordinates clearly so teammates can follow a choice.
Build turn-taking and tactical discussion as teams decide where to claim territory.
howItWorks: Two teams take turns answering questions and choosing an open sector on the board.
The board labels rows and columns from A to H and 1 to 8. Empty cells show their coordinate so a picker can call it aloud.
Choose speaking, written, or both question modes. Questions and options are shown at a size designed for a shared classroom screen.
A successful capture animates a plane across the board and lights the new sector. The tug-of-war bar tracks territory, and the winning line flashes when a team connects four.
teacherUseCases: Use a topic or question set from the current unit and pause before each pick so teammates can recommend a coordinate.
Ask students to say the coordinate and explain their team strategy before committing to a sector.

faq.q: How does a team win Sector Strike?
faq.a: Teams answer questions to claim sectors and try to connect four claimed cells in a row on the 8-by-8 board.

faq.q: Can students call their move aloud?
faq.a: Yes. Each empty sector displays a coordinate such as B4, and the board is designed so students can call the location clearly during a shared-screen lesson.
The game offers speaking only, written only, or both. The selected mode shapes whether students answer aloud, submit on phones, or use both approaches.

faq.q: What does the board show during play?
faq.a: A large radar-style board shows claimed territory, a team tug-of-war bar tracks progress, and a capture animation marks new sectors.
